newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic welcomes US troop commitment.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic welcomes US troop commitment.

text.p: Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic welcomed President Bill Clinton's announcement on Friday that U.S. troops would participate in a follow-up force in Bosnia next year.
"The presence of foreigners is not a joy for any country but when you have to have foreign troops in Bosnia... I would choose them to be Americans," he told Bosnian state television.
"With them we had the best cooperation so far without problems. If IFOR is to stay in Bosnia its good to have a significant number of American soldiers."

Earlier in Washington, Clinton said the United States had agreed in principle to take part in a follow-up international military force to help cement peace in Bosnia next year. He said this could amount to around 8,500 U.S. troops.
The mandate of the 50,000-strong NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) expires in December as scheduled under the Dayton peace accord.
Clinton had told the Republican-dominated Congress last December he would pull out U.S. troops before the end of 1996.
About one-third of the contigent are American soldiers and U.S. allies have warned they would not stay on in Bosnia if the Americans pulled out.
Clinton's decision paves way for NATO ambassadors to instruct their military on Monday to prepare for a force of betwen 25,000 and 30,000 troops to stay in Bosnia next year.
"We have expected IFOR2 to be half of the number of IFOR1. If half of the Americans stay then it's a bit beyond our expectations," Izetbegovic said.

Clinton's statement came a day after Bosnia's three co-presidents agreed with world powers meeting in Paris on a detailed plan to stabilise the peace in the former Yugoslav republic over the next two years as a condition for continuing international aid.
There was still no reaction to Clinton's decision by the Bosnian Serb side.
